subject: Astro Labs trial: criteria, timeline & SDK integration checklist
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@astrolabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@astrolabs.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood trial next steps & success criteria

Hi Karthik / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Samir and I spoke with our engineering and data science leads and want to confirm a short trial to validate Redwood against three key goals before we commit to Dedicated capacity. High-level asks: 

- Success criteria (what we must see to consider the trial a win):
  • End-to-end latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 200ms for typical 256-token prompts
  • Functional correctness: classification accuracy >= 88% on our in-domain testset for the recommendations model
  • Cost guidance: projected per-1M-token cost estimate for streaming vs batch variants

- Trial timeline: looking to start the trial week of May 17 and run 3–4 weeks. We can be flexible but need clear milestones.
- Integration scope: primary work is embedding + streaming generation for a recommendation microservice. We need SDK examples (Python + Node) and the API routes you recommend for streaming + tool-calling to external retrieval services.
- Ownership: who from your side will be our technical point of contact for integration and who owns escalation?

Please send a short plan we can review (success criteria mapped to tests, proposed endpoints, timeline/milestones, and assigned owners). Also attach any light technical docs and an example test dataset format so our SRE/data team can prep.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product, Astro Labs

Attachments: (request) astrolabs_testset_v1.json (we will send after your confirmation)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@astrolabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood trial next steps & success criteria

Elena —

Great to connect. Per your asks, attached is a concise trial plan ("trial_scope_and_timeline.xlsx") and a short SDK quickstart (pdf) we typically use for streaming + embeddings. Below is a proposed acceptance plan and the implementation checklist we recommend for a focused 3-week trial (with a 1-week buffer if you want to run edge cases).

Proposed trial: 
- Week 0 (prep): share test dataset + security questionnaire; Redwood provides trial credentials and test harness.
- Week 1 (integration): SDK install + basic generate/streaming integration; validate connectivity and auth.
- Week 2 (exercise): run evaluation tests (latency, accuracy, cost sampling) against your testset.
- Week 3 (stability & handoff): run smoke load, collect metrics, run acceptance tests.

Success criteria (mapped to tests):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms on 256-token prompts under our default routing policy — test: 1k sample requests in the harness, measure p95.
- Accuracy: >= 88% classification accuracy on provided testset — test: run batch eval with ground-truth labels.
- Cost: provide projected per-1M-token cost for both streaming and batch using your observed token distributions — test: synthesize typical workload and run cost estimates.

Implementation details / recommended routes: 
- SDKs: Python (redwood.Client) and Node (redwood-js) — quickstart attached (sdk_quickstart.pdf).
- API routes we recommend for your flow: 
  • /v1/generate — standard (sync) generation for offline scoring
  • /v1/stream — streaming token-level responses for online recommendation snippets
  • /v1/embeddings — embedding generation for retrieval and similarity
  • tool-calling: Redwood supports structured tool outputs and function-calling via the /v1/tools endpoint and can call back to your retrieval endpoint with a signed webhook.

Ownership (proposed): 
- Technical lead (integration & escalation): Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwood.ai) — will run SDK sessions and own the integration runbook.
- Commercial lead: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.ai) — pricing, credits, deal coordination.
- Internal engineering reviewer: Marissa Cole — will help with model-on-boarding checks and test harness.

Next steps: 
1) Elena/Samir: confirm trial start week (May 17 is fine for us).
2) Share testset format by EOD Monday so Dev can pre-stage evaluation harness.
3) We'll schedule a 60-minute integration session (Dev + your eng lead) for the first day of Week 1.

I attached: trial_scope_and_timeline.xlsx (timeline + milestones), sdk_quickstart.pdf (Python/Node examples).

If that looks good, Ben will send the trial credit note and I will schedule the kickoff with Dev.

—Karthik
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben/Karthik — this plan looks good. Confirming: start week May 17. Samir and I will send the trimmed testset (astrolabs_testset_v1.json) and a short SRE checklist by Monday.

Couple quick clarifications: 
- For the latency test, do you have a recommended harness we should run from our region (us-east-1)?
- For tool-calling: we want Redwood to be able to call our retrieval API but only via a signed webhook. Please confirm whether your tool-calling model supports HMAC-signed webhooks and how we can provision keys.

–Elena

Elena / Samir — looking forward to the kickoff. Confirmed items below and a brief SDK checklist to get your eng team running quickly. Kickoff meeting scheduled: May 17, 10:00 AM ET (calendar invite sent).

Security contact: noted Priya Khatri (we'll send the SOC2 summary and the concise questionnaire to her today).

Light integration checklist (Python & Node):
- Create trial API key in console (we'll provision and you will pick up under Credentials > Trial).
- Install SDK: pip install redwood-client   OR   npm install @redwood/inference
- Quick sample (Python):
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key="REDACTED_TRIAL_KEY")
  # streaming example
  with client.stream("/v1/stream", model="rwd-llm-2-std", input="Recommend help articles for user X") as s:
      for token in s:
          print(token.text, end="")

- Tool-calling: we'll exchange an HMAC key for your webhook. Redwood will sign outbound calls with X-Redwood-Signature and you can verify using the shared secret (we'll provision via the console's secret manager).
- Latency harness: we will share a small load script (k6 + python wrapper) in the drive folder; run it from a staging host in us-east-1 and post results to the harness run sheet.

Attachments uploaded to shared folder: trial_scope_and_timeline.xlsx, sdk_quickstart.pdf, astrolabs_testset_v1.json. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleKickoffDoc

If you hit any blockers before kickoff ping me directly (dev_patel@redwood.ai). I'll be online during the integration session and will stay after for 30 minutes for troubleshooting.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: trial_scope_and_timeline.xlsx (timeline + milestones), sdk_quickstart.pdf (Python/Node examples), astrolabs_testset_v1.json (sample-format)
